content.text: Purpose of AZM training

items: Equip participants with the knowledge and skills needed to properly administer Azithromycin to eligible children during campaign.
Ensure that participants understands proper dosing strategies and schedules for AZM medicines and can recognize when children need to be referred to health facilities.
Train Participants on safeguarding practices to protect children and vulnerable population during AZM drug administration.
Teach proper interpersonal communication technique to effectively educate caregivers about the administration of AZM and their potential side effects.
Provide hands-on practice through demonstration and role plays to build competence in all aspects of AZM drug administration.

content.text: Introduction to drug administration of Azithromycin

sections.title: Meaning of AZM

content.text: AZM means Azithromycin.

sections.title: Purpose of AZM drug administration

items: Azithromycin is a broad-based spectrum antibiotic which is effective in the prevention and treatment of various bacterial infections including acute lower respiratory tract infections, skin and soft tissue and gastro-enteric infections.
It offers broad benefits including protection against malaria caused by Plasmodium falciparum.
Azithromycin reduces childhood mortality by preventing and treating childhood infections such as pneumonia, diarrhoea and malaria.

content.statement: AZM prevents and treats pneumonia, diarrhoea and malaria in children 1-59 months

sections.title: Target age group for AZM administration

content.text: AZM Drug Administration is aimed protection children aged 1-59 months of age from childhood infections.

sections.title: Delivery strategies for AZM

items: The intervention is delivered through door-to-door approach by trained Community Drug Distributors, under the supervision of the CDD supervisors, LGA, State and National teams.
The AZM administration is done using the Technology app (DIGIT HCM) installed in the devices of the CDDs.

content.statement: AZM is delivered through door to door approach
AZM data is collected using Technology App

sections.title: What is AZM POS

content.text: AZM POS means Azithromycin Powdered Oral Suspension

sections.title: Duration of AZM drug administration

content.text: AZM is administered every six-months (Bi-annually) to children 1 to 59 months of age.

sections.title: What are the delivery platforms for AZM MDA

items: AZM MDA will leverage on the following child health interventions:
Neglected tropical disease (NTDs).
Polio Eradication Initiative campaign.
Seasonal Malaria Chemoprevention (SMC).
Maternal Newborn and Child health (MNCH).
Leveraging on these platforms will reduce operational costs, maximizes resources, enhance coverage by minimizing missed opportunities and maximizing health benefits to eligible populations.

sections.title: Key take away from module 1

content.heading: Key take away from module 1
content.text: 1. Azithromycin (AZM) is given to children within the age group of 1-59 months. 2. The medicine is for the prevention of pneumonia, diarrhoea and Malaria. 3. It is delivered using Door to door approach by CDDs under the supervision of the CDD supervisors. 4. The medicine is administered two times a year (every six months) using the DIGIT HCM app.

content.text: Age eligibility for Azithromycin (AZM) administration during campaign

sections.title: Eligibility age range for Children to receive AZM

items: AZM is given to only healthy children between 1 to 59 months of age.
Children who are less than one month or older than 59 months are not eligible.
Children who are 59 months old in round one should receive AZM but will not be eligible in the next round.
Neonates who are less than one month are not eligible.

content.statement: AZM is given to all children 1-59 months

sections.title: Why only children 1 to 59 months are eligible for AZM

items: The safety protocol for AZM has been established for children 1 months and above.
Younger children are more susceptible to potential side effects.
Children between 1 to 59 months are at the highest risk of severe malaria and other childhood infections
The age group experience the highest mortality rates from childhood infections.
It is easier to monitor and manage potential side effects in this age group (1-59 months).

sections.title: What are the ways to determine the age of a child

items: Ask to see the child's child health card.
Ask the caregiver the age of the child.
Use calendar of events.

sections.title: How to know if an infant is between 1 to 2 months

items: Cannot hold head and neck steady when held upright.

sections.title: How to know if an infant is between 3 to 4 months

items: Can hold head and neck steady when held upright.

sections.title: How to know if an infant is between 3 to 11 months

items: Can hold head and neck steady when held upright.
Can crawl.
Can sit without help.

sections.title: How do you know if a child is between 12 to 59 months

items: Can stand, walk or run.
Not able to raise the arm and touch the opposite side of the ear.
Not able to stand on one leg.

sections.title: How to know children older than 59months

items: Can raise the arm and touch the opposite side of the ear.
Can stand on one leg for 10 secs.
Can jump on one leg.
They are not eligible for AZM MDA.

content.text: How to determine child's age for AZM drug administration

content.caption: How to determine a child's age. Children 1 to 11 months: child 1 to 2 months cannot hold head and neck steady when upright; NOT newborn or less than one month; child 3 to 4 months can hold head and neck steady when upright; child 5 to 11 months can crawl and can sit without help. Child 12 to 59 months: can stand or walk; CANNOT raise arm and touch opposite ear; CANNOT stand or jump on one foot.

items: Advise the caregiver to take the child to the nearest health facility for further evaluation.

sections.title: Antibiotics in the last 28 days

content.heading: Antibiotics in the last 28 days
content.text: Do not give AZM to children who have taken antibiotics or similar medication in the last 28 days or 4 weeks or one month.

sections.title: Ask the caregiver

items: Has the child taken any medicine in the last 28 days or 4 weeks.
If yes, what medicine has the child taken in the past one month.
If possible, ask to see the packet for confirmation.

sections.title: Children not eligible for AZM MDA due to malnutrition: how to identify a child with severe acute malnutrition (Look and Feel Approach)

items: Visible severe wasting;
The child looks extremely thin.
The ribs, shoulder blades and bones are very prominent.
The arms and thigh look like “skin and bones” with little or no muscle or flesh.
The child's buttock may appear flat or baggy.

sections.title: Bilateral Pitting Oedema

items: Press gently with your thumb on the top of both feet for about 3 seconds.
If a pit remains after removing the thumb, oedema is present.
This indicates that the child has Kwashiorkor, a form of SAM.

content.statement: A child with SAM is not eligible for AZM

content.heading: AZM should not be given to the following children
content.text: Children from 60 months and older. Children that are allergic to AZM or similar antibiotics. Children who are sick or have fever. Children who have received AZM or other antibiotics in the last one month. Children who are currently taking AZM or other antibiotics. Children who cannot swallow.

Children with fever needs to be evaluated to avoid complications.

sections.title: Explain the steps for referral to the health facilities for children who are sick, or have severe acute malnutrition or suspected adverse reactions

items: Do not Give AZM.
Complete the top portion of the referral form.
Explain to the caregiver the reason for the referral and the need to respond immediately.

If the child has fever, or severe acute malnutrition, explain to the caregivers that the child could have malaria or other diseases and could get worse or even result in death if not treated immediately.
Tell the caregiver how to get to the nearest health facility.
Give AZM referral form to the caregiver to take to the health facility.
Explain to the caregiver that the health worker will evaluate the child at the facility.

content.text: Azithromycin Powdered Oral Suspension (AZM POS)

sections.title: Explain and show: Azithromycin POS

items: The Azithromycin (AZM) comes in small powdered Oral suspension (POS) bottle.
The medicine comes with a small dispensing cup for measuring accurate dose or volume of reconstituted AZM to be administered to eligible children.
The medicine will need to be reconstituted with 15ml of clean water to obtain 30ml AZM suspension.
Each bottle of AZM will be used to reach 4 children.

content.caption: 1. Check expiry date of the medicine. 2. Wash hand. 3. Provide clean water from the household. 4. Reconstitute AZM medicine. 5. Measure out AZM for dispensing.
content.alt: Five numbered pictures: a medicine bottle marked expiry date, hands washing under a tap, a measuring beaker of water, a CDD preparing AZM with a mother and child, and AZM suspension poured into a measuring cup.

content.text: Azithromycin drug administration protocol

sections.title: Explain and show: how to safely administer AZM

items: The CDD should check the expiry date of drug before reconstitution.
Wash hands with soap and water before administering AZM.
Limit AZM administration to 5 eligible children at a time.
Ask the caregiver to bring drinking water in a small cup.

sections.title: Steps for administering AZM

items: First, shake the AZM powder vigorously to loosen it.
Add 15ml of clean water and shake the bottle thoroughly to mix.

For children 1-11 months, determine the dose using the age-based dosing strategy (3-tier dosing schedule) as follows: 1-2 months will receive 2ml, 3-4 months will receive 3ml while 5-11 months will receive 4ml.

For children 12-59 months: The dosing pole will be used to measure their height (Height based dosing strategy). The measurement in cm is on one side of the pole while the corresponding dose to be administered to the child is indicated on the opposite side of the pole.
The DIGIT HCM app will indicate the dose to be administered when the age or height of the child is inputted into the app.
The CDD should measure out the accurate dose of AZM to be administered using the provided dispensing cup.
AZM should be administered to one child per time.
If the child vomits within 5 minutes after receiving AZM, the child should be redosed with the same dose according to their age or height.
Observe the child for 30 minutes after administration for any side effect or Suspected ADR for referral.

content.statement: The age or height of the child is used to calculate the dose of AZM to be given
There is no re-dosing in AZM administration

content.text: Azithromycin drug administration protocol

sections.title: How AZM Medicines are issued

items: OICs in the facilities will issue AZM medicine and other implementation tools to each CDD team at the beginning of each day of the implementation period.
CDD teams must meet the OIC every morning during the implementation period to request for AZM medicine needed for administration to the target population.
Each CDD team is expected to reach a total of 100 children each day during the 4 days distribution period

sections.title: What need to be returned to the OICs at the end of each day during MDA

items: All AZM bottles must be accounted for daily during the MDA.
All used and unused bottles of AZM medicines must be returned to the Health facility OIC.
Partially used AZM medicines remain viable for up to 2 to 3 days and must be reused before a new one is opened.

CDDs must measure the exact dose displayed on the DIGIT app because overdosing or under dosing will result in wastage that will affect drug reconciliation leading to accountability issues, and drug resistance.
CDD must ensure that dosing poles are returned to the health facility daily.
The OICs must check the technology app to know the number of children reached by each CDD team .
The OICs should document the distribution of AZM in the inventory control cards and all the empty bottles should be properly arranged in the cartons.

content.text: Correct positioning for administration of AZM

items: Ensure that the child is awake.
Sit the child upright to avoid spitting or vomiting.
Give medicine slowly with the dispensing cup.
Ensure that the child drinks ALL the medicine by rinsing the cup with a small amount of water and give to swallow again
Do not force the child to swallow the medicines by holding the child's head and neck backwards or pinching the nose.
Repeat steps 3,4,5 and 6 until all the children in the group have received AZM.
Redose if the child vomits within 5 minutes of AZM administration.
The CDD team should observe the child for 30mins for any side effect or suspected adverse reaction.

sections.title: STEP 1: Steps for mixing and administering AZM POS. Gather the following required materials

items: Azithromycin POS
Safe drinking water in a clean cup.
A calibrated measuring cup.

sections.title: Check the expiry date

content.heading: Check the expiry date
content.text: Check the expiry date of the AZM POS before administration. (Do not use if expired).

items: Shake the powder to loosen the contents.
Tap the bottle gently to loosen the dry powder before adding water.
Measure and add 15ml of water to obtain 30ml final volume of AZM suspension.
Use the provided measuring cup to add the correct amount of water.
Close the bottle tightly and shake well for at least 30 secs to ensure that the powder dissolves completely into a smooth suspension.
Shake again before each use to maintain consistency.

sections.title: Determine and administer the correct dose

content.text: The dose of AZM to be administered depends on the child's age: For Children 1-11 months: use age-based dosing Strategy (3-tier schedule) and for children 12-59months; use height based dosing strategy by measuring their height with a dosing pole.

content.caption: AZM is given slowly and the child properly positioned
content.alt: A mother in a green hijab holds a baby upright and gives medicine from a small cup.

content.text: Section 2: Call-in-data reporting during AZM MDA (for CDDs and OICs)
Introduction to call-in data in AZM MDA

sections.title: Implementation steps

items: CDD teams should document every child reached according to the two age categories: 1–11 months and 12–59 months.

At the end of each day at the health facility, each CDD team should total the number of children reached in both age categories (1–11 months and 12–59 months). These totals must correspond with the number of children recorded in the DIGIT HCM app.
The Officer-in-Charge (OIC) should aggregate the totals from all CDD teams in the facility for each age (1–11 months and 12–59 months).
OICs should download the call-in data form from Kobo Collect into their devices for data entry.
Each health facility has a unique Facility ID, which should be used to access the appropriate form.
The aggregated totals for each age category (1–11 months and 12–59 months) should be entered into the Kobo Collect form and submit.

sections.title: For Integrated campaigns (AZM+MUAC; AZM+ MNCHW – VITAMIN A, MUAC, ANC; Albendazole, etc)

items: CDD teams should document every child reached according to the two age categories: 6 –11 months and 12–59 months.

At the end of each day at the health facility, each CDD team should total the number of children reached in both age categories (6 –11 months and 12–59 months). These totals must correspond with the number of children recorded in the Kobo Collect tool or DIGIT HCM app.
The Officer-in-Charge (OIC) should aggregate the totals from all CDD teams in the facility for each age (6–11 months and 12–59 months).
OICs should download the call-in data form from Kobo Collect into their devices for data entry.
Each health facility has a unique Facility ID, which should be used to access the appropriate form.
The aggregated totals for each age category (6–11 months and 12–59 months) should be entered into the Kobo Collect form and submit.
Call-in data must be submitted daily throughout the implementation period including mop-up.

content.alt: Several people bend over open cardboard cartons, sorting white AZM bottles.

content.text: Section 3: Procedures for Azithromycin drug accountability and reconciliation in the health facility
Procedures for AZM drug accountability and reconciliation

sections.title: Steps for AZM drug accountability (Explain)

items: OICs should confirm and ensure proper documentation of AZM bottles received in the facility using the Issue and Receipt Voucher and Inventory Control Card.

OICs are to issue to the CDD teams, the quantities of Azithromycin bottles needed to meet their daily target both physically and digitally through the technology app. Please note that the quantity of AZM bottles issued digitally in the app must correspond to the number of physical bottles issued.
All the physical quantities issued to each CDD teams must be documented in the Inventory control card.
CDD teams are to ensure that the physical bottles of AZM are kept safely in the AZM bags provided to avoid unintended losses
In the field, the CDD teams are to ensure that each bottle of AZM POS is reconstituted with exactly 15 ml of water.
During dispensing, CDDs are to ensure that the exact dose displayed on the app is measured using the calibrated cups to avoid over or underdosing.
Any redosing due to vomiting within 5 minutes must be properly captured in the app for accountability.
CDD teams are to ensure that each opened bottle is exhausted before opening another AZM bottle for reconstitution.

sections.title: Steps for AZM drug reconciliation and accountability: continues

items: CDD teams should separate the empty AZM bottles from all unopened or unused bottles in the AZM bag.

In the facility, OICs should count the number of empty bottles returned by each CDD team and multiply this by 4 to get the number of children to be reached. The number is then compared with the number of actual children reached in the DIGIT HCM app.
The number of unopened and empty bottles of AZM returned by each CDD team must correspond to the number of bottles issued to them in the morning by the OIC.
Both empty and unopened bottles should be arranged in separate cartons in the health facility for ease of accountability.
All missing bottles should be escalated to the LGA logistician and the NTD coordinator for possible investigation.
All AZM bottles (used and unused bottles) should be arranged in cartons and returned to the LGA store within 3 days after implementation to avoid pilferages and diversion.

sections.title: Key take away for participants

content.heading: Key take away for participants
content.text: CDD teams and OICs are responsible for Azithromycin drug accountability at the health facility level. Lack of accountability will lead to pilferages and diversion that will result in AZM drug influx into the markets and community drug sales outlets. The reconciliation and accountability of AZM Drugs and other commodities should be conducted daily between the CDD teams and the OICs in the health facility at the end of the day. All AZM bottles (used and unused bottles) should be arranged in cartons for easy accountability.

content.text: Introduction to cohort tracking in AZM

items: One of the critical challenges in AZM implementation is ensuring that eligible children are retained throughout the entire campaign period.
Retention tracking becomes paramount to assess the program's effectiveness and ensure consistent protection against malaria.
AZM Cohort Tracking addresses this challenge by systematically monitoring and evaluating the progress of individual children enrolled in the program across multiple treatment rounds.

Through innovative tools like the DIGIT HCM App, data managers can track the same cohort of beneficiaries over successive rounds, enabling comprehensive evaluation of the program's impact on preventing key childhood diseases like diarrhea, pneumonia and malaria

sections.title: What is cohort tracking in AZM?

content.text: In the context of Safety and Antimicrobial Resistance of Mass Administration of Azithromycin in Children 1–59 months in Nigeria (SARMAAN II), cohort tracking means following groups of children who receive Azithromycin during each campaign round, so that their health outcomes can be monitored over time.

sections.title: Why Cohort Tracking in AZM Campaigns

items: Measure effectiveness: By tracking cohorts of children who received AZM, researchers and program managers can see how well the intervention reduces under 5 morbidity and mortality:
Monitor safety: Cohorts help identify any side effects or adverse reactions to the drugs.
Evaluate coverage & adherence: Tracking shows whether children consistently receive all rounds treatment during campaign periods.
Policy decisions: Evidence from cohorts guides governments and partners on whether to expand, adjust, or improve AZM campaigns.

sections.title: Who are responsible for cohort tracking

items: Cohort tracking is not the job of one person; it's a chain of responsibility.
CDDs gather the raw data,
M&E teams analyze it, and
policymakers use the insights to improve AZM Campaign.
CDDs administer AZM and record which children received on DIGIT HCM.
Supervisors ensure data is collected correctly and cohorts are defined.
M&E teams analyze cohort data; tracking drop out and provide timely feedback.
Government and IPs uses the findings to adjust campaign strategies.

content.caption: Cohort Tracking Responsibility Flow: Community Drug Distributors (administer treatment, collect data) → CDDs supervisors, health facility supervisors, Nat'l, State & LGA team (monitor & verify data) → State & Country M&E team (analyze & compare cohorts) → Government & Partners (policy decisions, program adjustments). Data collection (field work) → data reporting (supervision) → analysis & reports (data analysis) → policy action.

content.text: Introduction to safeguarding

sections.title: What safeguarding means and why it is important

items: Safeguarding refers to the commitment of an organization to ensure that staff and program activities do not harm children and vulnerable adults or expose them to potential abuse, harm, risk or exploitation.
It involves the protection of the rights and dignity of all individual especially children and vulnerable adults to ensure that they are free from abuse, harm and exploitation.

content.statement: Safeguarding means protecting only children from harm and abuse

sections.title: Safeguarding during AZM Campaign: Safeguarding is

items: An organization's resolve to safeguarding children and vulnerable adults from harm and abuse during campaign.
This include upholding and protecting the rights and dignity of all individuals with particular attention to children.

sections.title: Examples of safeguarding

items: Respectful interaction with caregivers and their families.
Educating community members on the benefits of AZM.
Addressing concerns of caregivers regarding AZM Campaign.
Ensuring informed consent from caregivers.
Handling AZM medicines safely during AZM Campaign.

content.statement: Safeguarding entails interacting respectfully with caregiver

sections.title: Protection during AZM Campaign

items: Protection means taking action when children or vulnerable individuals are found to be at risk or experience harm.
It involves specific measures to address immediate safety concerns such as:
Ensuring that only eligible children receive AZM.
Administering the correct dose.
Preventing overdosing during MDA.
Referring sick children to the nearest health facility.

content.statement: Protection involves specific measures to address immediate safety concerns during AZM MDA

content.text: Safeguarding case studies

sections.title: Safeguarding during AZM Campaign extends to the following

items: Ensuring the safe selection of Community volunteers. The selection of CDDs should be carried out with active involvement of the community to guarantee that those chosen truly represent the community, uphold integrity and are motivated primarily by the community interest.
Caregivers have the right to give informed consent, treated with dignity and respect, be informed of their rights and know the names of both the CDD and their supervisors.
Caregivers must be provided with complete and accurate information including potential risks and steps to take in the event of any adverse reaction.

Caregivers should have the means to contact someone for support, advice, or to raise concerns and complaints if they feel misinformed or maltreated. The consent form should list few designated contacts they can reach out to for assistance.

sections.title: CDDs must not force AZM

content.heading: CDDs must not force AZM
content.text: CDDs must not force AZM on caregivers or treat children harshly.

sections.title: Reporting safeguarding issues

items: All safeguarding issues should be reported to the CDD supervisors or health facility OICs who will scale it up to the NTD coordinator of the LGA team and partners.

CDDs are required to report any cases or suspected cases of violence or neglect involving eligible children to the health facility OIC, who will in turn escalate these to malaria consortium through the appropriate MoH structures.
All safeguarding issues should be reported to concenrns@malariaconsortium.org.
